import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
cameras = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a bar chart to compare the average price by sensor type
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', data=cameras, ci=None)
plt.title('Average Price by Sensor Type')
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type')
plt.ylabel('Average Price (USD)')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a histogram to display the distribution of megapixels
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.histplot(cameras['megapixels'], kde=True, bins=20)
plt.title('Distribution of Megapixels')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Frequency')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output2.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between price and megapixels
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.scatterplot(x='megapixels', y='price_usd', data=cameras)
plt.title('Price vs Megapixels')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output3.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
